title: Directional effects of the Unruh effect on steering harvesting
authors: Shu-Min Wu, Rui-Yang Xu, Zhihong Liu
abstract: We investigate directional quantum steering harvesting by two uniformly accelerated non-identical Unruh-DeWitt detectors coupled to a massless scalar field in the Minkowski vacuum. We show that the Unruh effect does not simply degrade harvested steering, but can reshape its directionality in a strongly parameter-dependent manner. At low detector energy scales, acceleration predominantly suppresses steering, whereas at higher energy scales, moderate acceleration can enhance steering and even activate an initially absent steering direction. Most strikingly, within a finite acceleration window, the Unruh effect enhances steering in one direction while simultaneously suppressing it in the opposite direction, revealing an intrinsically directional influence of relativistic acceleration. Detector non-identicality provides an additional control mechanism: a moderate energy-gap mismatch can enhance or activate one steering direction while suppressing the reverse one, whereas sufficiently large energy-gap mismatch suppresses the harvested steering. Moreover, the maximal steering asymmetry approximately marks the transition from two-way to one-way steering. Our results establish relativistic acceleration and detector non-identicality as means of controlling the strength and directionality of vacuum-harvested quantum correlations.
summary: This theoretical study examines how the Unruh effect dictates the directionality of quantum steering harvested from the vacuum by two accelerated detectors. The key finding is that relativistic acceleration and mismatches in detector energy levels can actively control this directionality, enhancing steering in one direction while suppressing it in the opposite. This establishes acceleration and detector design as tools for manipulating vacuum quantum correlations.
main_problem: The paper investigates how the Unruh effect influences the directionality of quantum steering harvested from the vacuum by two non-identical detectors.
main_result: The Unruh effect can reshape steering directionality, allowing acceleration and detector non-identicality to control the strength and direction of vacuum-harvested quantum correlations.
method: The authors calculate the reduced density matrix perturbatively up to second order in the coupling strength, analyzing directional steering measures derived from auxiliary states.
model_or_system: The system consists of two non-identical Unruh-DeWitt detectors coupled to a massless scalar field in the Minkowski vacuum, undergoing uniform acceleration.
key_observables: Directional quantum steering measures ($S_{B	o A}$ and $S_{A	o B}$), and the steering asymmetry ($S_{\Delta}^{AB}$).
important_parameters: Acceleration ($a$), detector separation ($L$), and the energy-gap difference ($\Delta\Omega = \Omega_B - \Omega_A$).
main_assumptions: Calculations are performed perturbatively up to second order in the coupling strength ($\lambda$), and the field is assumed to be in the Minkowski vacuum.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the dependence of steering measures on detector separation, acceleration, and energy-gap mismatch, showing non-monotonic behavior and regime transitions.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by defining the system and observables, analyzing the dependence on separation, then acceleration, and finally detailing the control mechanisms offered by detector non-identicality.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete, controllable mechanism (acceleration/non-identicality) to manipulate quantum correlations derived from vacuum fluctuations, which is highly relevant to understanding quantum resource extraction in curved or accelerating spacetimes.
